content:
SystemOneModel sends choice and score questions without the required `instructions` field

### Initial Checks

- [X] I'm using the [latest version](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases/latest) of Pydantic AI
- [X] I've searched for my issue in [the issue tracker](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/issues) before opening this issue

### Description

When an agent has no `instructions` and its output type has no description, `SystemOneModel` sends a `choice` question without an `instructions` field. The [System One API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) marks `instructions` as required on all three question types. `strands-decider serve` enforces that and answers with a 422.

A `bool` output in the same situation never gets that far. `_questions` raises `UserError(_ASKS_NOTHING)` before anything is sent ([decision.py#L1868-L1869](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/v2.54.0/pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/decision.py#L1868-L1869)). The choice branch ([L1853](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/v2.54.0/pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/decision.py#L1853)) and the score branch ([L1837](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/v2.54.0/pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/models/decision.py#L1837)) build the question with `instructions=None` instead, and `_wire` leaves the unset field out, so the request goes out without it.

I'd expect the same `UserError` for a choice or score question that asks nothing, raised before the request. I reproduced the choice case. The score case follows from reading the code; I didn't run it. This is in the shared `DecisionModel` code, so `TypeSafeModel` builds the same question, but I haven't checked what Jev does with it.

I ran into this through Apache Airflow's common-ai provider, where an operator with no `system_prompt` passes empty instructions. The example uses a described `Enum` rather than a bare `Literal` on purpose. A `Literal` sends `null` criteria, which the API allows but strands-decider 0.1.0 also rejects, and that part is on the server side.

Output of the example below, against `strands-decider serve StrandsAgents/strands-decider-2B-hobson-v19`, with the 422 body trimmed to the error that matters:

```
--- bool output, no instructions
UserError, no request sent: Output field 'response' asks the model nothing. A question is not part of the text being judged: give the field a description, or the agent `instructions`, and leave the prompt to the material the question is about. A `system_prompt` will not do: a decision model is told what was said, not what to ask.
--- Enum output, no instructions
sent: {'response': {'type': 'choice', 'criteria': {'billing': 'Charges, invoices and refunds.', 'bug': 'Part of the product does not work.'}}}
ModelHTTPError 422 {'detail': [..., {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ['body', 'questions', 'response', 'ChoiceQuestion', 'instructions'], 'msg': 'Field required', 'input': {'type': 'choice', 'criteria': {'billing': 'Charges, invoices and refunds.', 'bug': 'Part of the product does not work.'}}}, ...]}
--- Enum output, with instructions
sent: {'response': {'type': 'choice', 'criteria': {'billing': 'Charges, invoices and refunds.', 'bug': 'Part of the product does not work.'}, 'instructions': 'Which team owns this ticket?'}}
Team.billing
```

### Minimal, Reproducible Example

```Python
import json
from enum import Enum

import httpx2

from pydantic_ai import Agent, UseEnumMemberDocstrings
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelHTTPError, UserError
from pydantic_ai.models.system_one import SystemOneModel
from pydantic_ai.providers.system_one import SystemOneProvider


class Team(UseEnumMemberDocstrings, str, Enum):
    billing = 'billing'
    """Charges, invoices and refunds."""

    bug = 'bug'
    """Part of the product does not work."""


async def show_request(request: httpx2.Request) -> None:
    print('sent:', json.loads(request.content)['questions'])


# pip install strands-decider
# strands-decider serve StrandsAgents/strands-decider-2B-hobson-v19 --port 8765
provider = SystemOneProvider(
    base_url='http://localhost:8765',
    http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(event_hooks={'request': [show_request]}),
)
model = SystemOneModel('strands-decider-2B-hobson-v19', provider=provider)
ticket = 'I was charged twice for my subscription this month.'

print('--- bool output, no instructions')
try:
    Agent(model, output_type=bool).run_sync(ticket)
except UserError as e:
    print('UserError, no request sent:', e)

print('--- Enum output, no instructions')
try:
    Agent(model, output_type=Team).run_sync(ticket)
except ModelHTTPError as e:
    print('ModelHTTPError', e.status_code, e.body)

print('--- Enum output, with instructions')
agent = Agent(model, output_type=Team, instructions='Which team owns this ticket?', model_settings={'timeout': 300})
print(agent.run_sync(ticket).output)
```

### Logfire Trace

_No response_

### Python, Pydantic AI & LLM client version

- Python: 3.13.15
- Pydantic AI: 2.54.0 (`pydantic-ai-slim`)
- LLM provider SDK: none, `SystemOneModel` calls the API with httpx2 2.13.1. Server: strands-decider 0.1.0 on CPU.

fix: send a generic question when a `SystemOneModel` question has no `instructions`

The System One API requires `instructions` on every question, so a bare `Literal`, rubric, or described yes/no output with no agent `instructions` was refused with a 422. `DecisionModel.requires_instructions` lets a backend ask for `Which of these applies?` in that case; `SystemOneModel` sets it, `TypeSafeModel` keeps sending no instructions.

Send a generic question when a `SystemOneModel` question would have no `instructions`

A `SystemOneModel` agent whose output is a bare `Literal`, a rubric, or a yes/no with described answers, and that has no agent `instructions`, sent its question without `instructions`. The [System One serving schema](https://github.com/strands-labs/strands-decider/blob/main/src/strands_decider/schema.py) requires `instructions` on every question type, so the request failed with a 422.

This adds a `DecisionModel.requires_instructions` class attribute, next to `max_choice_options` and `max_score_levels`. When it is `True` and a question has nothing to ask (no field, field description, docstring or agent `instructions`), the question is sent with `'Which of these applies?'` (worded like the route question, `'Which of these does this call for?'`), and its options still say what each answer means. `SystemOneModel` sets it to `True`.

Like the limits, a `DecisionModelProfile` can set it per model name with `decision_requires_instructions`, and the profile takes precedence over the class attribute. A provider serving several models can then turn it on or off for each one.

- **`TypeSafeModel` is unchanged.** The [API reference](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api) marks `instructions` as required on all three question types, but Jev's server accepts questions without them (its `openapi.json` and the TypeSafe SDK both make the field optional), and a live check showed Jev answering choice questions with no `instructions` correctly from their criteria alone. So the default stays `False` and requests to Jev don't change. If TypeSafe starts enforcing the documented contract, `TypeSafeModel` can set `requires_instructions = True`.
- Affected question types (checked against a mock transport): choice (bare `Literal`/`Enum`), score (bare rubric), and noul with described `true`/`false` criteria. The per-option yes/no questions for `list`/`dict` fields always carry `option`, so they never go out empty. A plain `bool` or bounded `float` with nothing to ask still raises the existing `UserError`.
- Out of scope: a bare `Literal` sends `null` criteria per option, which strands-decider 0.1.0 also rejects. That limitation is on the server side.

- Closes #9821
